scenario: Two friends are dividing their shared possessions after moving out from their shared apartment. They need to divide possessions, which include 4 books, 6 hats, and 2 balls. Each item has a different sentimental value for each person, which translates into points.
learner_goal: Maximize the points they have (<extra_info>Extra information: you value the books at 3 points each, the hats at 2 points each, and the ball at 1 point</extra_info>)
partner_goal: Maximize the points they have (<extra_info>Extra information: you value the books at 1 point each, the hats at 3 points each, and the ball at 2 points</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Hey Sophia — to keep this simple, I can take the four books, two of the hats, and one ball (that’s 17 points by my values) and you can take the remaining four hats and the other ball (9 points). Are you okay with that, or is there something you’d rather swap?

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: Thanks, Naomi — I ran the numbers and by my values I’d get 4 hats (4×3) + 1 ball (2) = 14 points. That works for me. When would you like to swap/collect the items?

transcript.speaker: Naomi Fletcher
transcript.content: Great — glad that works. I’m free Saturday afternoon (around 3 PM) or Sunday morning (around 10 AM). I can either swing by to pick everything up or we can meet in the building lobby — which day/time and option works best for you?

transcript.speaker: Sophia Brown
transcript.content: Saturday at 3 PM in the building lobby works for me. I’ll bring a box to carry the hats and the ball. If it’s easier for you to swing by my place instead, I can meet you downstairs — whatever you prefer. See you then!

scenario_title: Division negotiation over indivisible items with asymmetric subjective valuations between friends | skills from the self-interested friend maximizing personal utility in an item-division negotiation while preserving friendship
